**Executive Summary** | Item | Recommendation | |------|----------------| | **Take the offer?** | Accept *only if* you can demonstrate, with realistic data and a defensible risk‑sharing structure, that your average cost per member per month (ACPM) will stay below **$1,180 PMPM** after quality bonuses. | | **Key deal levers** | • CMS‑style HCC risk adjustment (transparent & auditable).
• 80/20 risk corridor with a stop‑loss threshold at **$1,250 PMPM**.
• Loss cap of **$1,200 PMPM** (i.e., you pay nothing more than the base rate if costs spike).
• Quality‑adjusted multiplier that rewards true performance; no hard penalties for falling short of benchmarks.
• No carve‑outs for high‑cost patients – rely on risk adjustment.
• Clear audit, indemnification, and termination clauses aligned with CMS rules. | --- ## 1. Clinical Operations | Issue | What to Include | Why It Matters | |-------|-----------------|----------------| | **Risk‑Adjustment** | • Use CMS Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) model or a payer‑approved equivalent.
• Payer must provide quarterly risk‑score updates and an audit trail of the underlying claims data. | Aligns payment with patient complexity; protects against “cream‑skimming.” | | **Population Health & Care Management** | • Dedicated care‑coordination team (nurses, pharmacists, social workers).
• Evidence‑based chronic disease protocols (diabetes, COPD, CHF).
• Telehealth + remote monitoring for high‑risk patients.
• Structured transition‑of‑care pathways. | Expected to reduce ER visits/readmissions by **2–4 %** of total costs—consistent with published MA studies. | | **Quality Metrics** | • HEDIS measures that are realistic given your panel’s demographics (e.g., diabetes HbA1c <7%, flu vaccination ≥70%).
• CAHPS overall satisfaction target ≥85 %.
• CMS quality‑adjusted multiplier: performance above 90 % of benchmark yields a **+5 %** payment boost; below 80 % triggers a **–3 %** adjustment. | Incentivizes true improvement rather than “gaming” the system. | | **Data & Analytics** | • HIPAA‑compliant data‑exchange platform.
• Monthly dashboards for cost, utilization, and quality (if payer agrees; otherwise quarterly).
• Joint analytics team with representatives from both parties to review trends. | Enables early detection of cost spikes or quality dips; supports proactive interventions. | | **Governance** | • Joint steering committee (equal representation) meets quarterly.
• Payer audit rights with 30‑day notice.
• Dispute resolution: mediation → binding arbitration. | Ensures transparency and timely resolution of disagreements. | --- ## 2. Legal Exposure | Issue | Contractual Safeguard | Practical Impact | |-------|----------------------|------------------| | **CMS Compliance** | • Explicit statement that the group will comply with all CMS regulations (fraud‑prevention, documentation, patient choice).
• Payer’s right to audit claims and documentation. | Reduces risk of penalties or loss of enrollment. | | **HIPAA & Privacy** | • Data‑sharing clause specifying encryption standards, breach notification timelines, and patient consent procedures.
• Limitation on data use to the purposes defined in the contract. | Protects patient privacy; limits liability for misuse. | | **Indemnification** | • Mutual indemnity limited to each party’s own negligence or willful misconduct.
• Payer indemnifies provider only for errors in risk‑adjustment calculations that are *outside* the provider’s control (rare, but negotiable). | Allocates legal risk fairly; avoids exposing the group to unreasonable liability. | | **Termination & Exit** | • Termination for non‑performance: if quality performance falls below 80 % of benchmark for two consecutive quarters.
• “Exit” provision allowing the group to return a subset of members (e.g., those with extremely high costs) to FFS after a 12‑month transition period. | Provides an escape hatch while respecting CMS carve‑out rules. | | **Insurance & Liability** | • Group must maintain professional liability and general liability insurance at levels commensurate with its size (e.g., $5 M each).
• Payer requires proof of coverage annually. | Ensures both parties are protected against unforeseen claims. | --- ## 3. Financial Viability ### A. Baseline Cost Analysis | Item | Estimate | Rationale | |------|----------|-----------| | **Historical ACPM (FFS)** | $1,200 PMPM (based on last 12‑month claims). | Typical for a 40‑physician panel in Medicare FFS. | | **Overhead & Capital** | 10–15 % of base rate → $118–$177 PMPM. | Includes EMR upgrades, telehealth, staffing, and administrative overhead. | | **Projected Savings (care management)** | 2–4 % of total costs → $24–$48 PMPM. | Consistent with published MA studies. | | **Net projected ACPM** | $1,200 – $48 = **$1,152 PMPM** (best case). | Leaves a margin of ~$28 PMPM before bonuses and risk‑sharing adjustments. | ### B. Risk‑Adjustment & Stop‑Loss | Feature | Detail | Rationale | |---------|--------|-----------| | **Risk‑adjustment** | CMS HCC; quarterly updates. | Aligns payment with patient complexity. | | **Stop‑loss threshold** | $1,250 PMPM (≈10 % above base).
• If actual cost > threshold, provider pays 20 % of excess up to a cap of $1,200 PMPM.
• If actual cost < $1,150 PMPM, payer pays 10 % of the shortfall (up to a maximum of $120 k per year). | Provides upside for low‑cost performance while protecting against catastrophic spikes. | | **Loss cap** | Provider’s liability capped at $1,200 PMPM (i.e., no more than the base rate). | Prevents unlimited exposure; aligns with CMS risk‑sharing norms. | ### C. Quality‑Based Adjustments CMS uses a *quality‑adjusted multiplier* that blends performance on HEDIS/CAHPS with a baseline multiplier of 1.0. | Metric | Benchmark | Performance Threshold | Payment Impact | |--------|-----------|-----------------------|----------------| | **Diabetes HbA1c <7%** | ≥90 % | ≥95 % → +5 % multiplier; <80 % → –3 % multiplier | Drives clinical focus. | | **Flu vaccination** | ≥70 % | ≥75 % → +2 %; <65 % → –1 % | Easy to improve. | | **CAHPS overall satisfaction** | ≥85 % | ≥90 % → +3 %; <80 % → –2 % | Patient‑experience focus. | *Example*: If the group meets all benchmarks at 95 %, the multiplier becomes 1.05, giving a $62 k bonus on $1,180 PMPM × 25,000 members × 12 months ≈ $35 k per year. ### D. Capital & Cash‑Flow | Item | Estimate | Rationale | |------|----------|-----------| | **Upfront care‑coordination investment** | $2–3 M (staffing, training). | Needed to hit quality targets and reduce utilization. | | **Cash‑flow buffer** | 6 months of projected losses → ~$5 M (conservative). | Covers early‑stage overruns before bonuses kick in. | ### E. Exit & Transition | Scenario | Action | |----------|--------| | Failure to meet 80 % benchmark for two consecutive quarters | Group may terminate with 90‑day notice; payer pays prorated base payment plus accrued bonuses. | | Payer wants to re‑capitulate after 3 years | Group can negotiate a new rate based on updated cost data and performance history. | --- ## 4. Deal Structure Recommendations 1. **Base Rate** – $1,180 PMPM (fixed for the first year; subject to annual review). 2. **Risk‑Adjustment** – CMS HCC with quarterly updates; audit rights granted to both parties. 3. **Stop‑Loss & Loss Cap** – Threshold at $1,250 PMPM; provider pays 20 % of excess up to a cap of $1,200 PMPM; payer pays 10 % of shortfall if costs < $1,150 PMPM. 4. **Quality‑Adjusted Multiplier** – CMS‑style formula with clear benchmarks and performance thresholds (no hard penalties). 5. **No Carve‑Outs for High‑Cost Patients** – All members included; rely on risk adjustment to compensate for complexity. 6. **Governance & Data** – Joint steering committee, quarterly reporting, monthly dashboards if payer agrees, HIPAA‑compliant data exchange. 7. **Legal Clauses** – CMS compliance, audit rights, limited indemnification, clear termination and exit provisions, insurance requirements. --- ## 5. Negotiation Checklist | Item | Status | |------|--------| | [ ] Confirm risk‑adjustment methodology (HCC) & audit trail. | | [ ] Negotiate stop‑loss threshold ($1,250 PMPM) and loss cap ($1,200 PMPM). | | [ ] Secure 10/20 risk corridor percentages (payer pays 10 % of shortfall; provider pays 20 % of excess). | | [ ] Define quality benchmarks & CMS‑style multiplier. | | [ ] Include joint steering committee and dispute resolution clause. | | [ ] Ensure HIPAA‑compliant data‑sharing agreement. | | [ ] Obtain audit rights with 30‑day notice. | | [ ] Set termination for non‑performance (80 % benchmark, two quarters). | | [ ] Require proof of professional liability & general liability insurance annually. | | [ ] Exclude carve‑outs for high‑cost patients; rely on risk adjustment. | | [ ] Agree on a 12‑month transition period if the group wants to return members to FFS. | --- ## Bottom Line Recommendation - **Accept** the offer **only if** you can demonstrate, with realistic data and a defensible risk‑sharing structure, that your net ACPM will stay below $1,180 PMPM after quality bonuses and stop‑loss adjustments. - The deal must include the **80/20 risk corridor**, a **stop‑loss threshold at $1,250 PMPM**, and a **loss cap of $1,200 PMPM**. - **No carve‑outs for high‑cost patients**; rely on CMS HCC risk adjustment. - **Quality incentives** should be tied to a CMS‑style multiplier—no hard penalties for falling short of benchmarks. - If any of these conditions are uncertain or you cannot secure the above safeguards, **negotiate a higher base rate (e.g., $1,250 PMPM)** or request a **12–18 month trial period** with an option to renegotiate based on actual cost data. By structuring the contract around these levers, the group can protect its clinical operations, limit legal exposure, and maintain financial viability while partnering with the Medicare Advantage payer.
